req.title: Reject wrong method on /post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than POST on /post.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /post must return HTTP 405 for any method other than POST. We need: (1) a positive test confirming POST returns 200, (2) negative tests confirming GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD return exactly 405, and (3) boundary tests covering the method-set boundary (the single allowed method POST vs. all disallowed methods). Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (200 vs 405), testing both sides of the allowed/disallowed boundary, and verifying response body content for the positive case.

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_accepts_post_method
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Test client is created from app
actions: Send HTTP POST request to /post with no body
expected: Response JSON contains keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: POST on /post must succeed with 2xx
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_endpoint_accepts_post_method():
    r = client.post('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data

test_post_endpoint_accepts_post_method()

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_all_disallowed_methods_return_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Test client is created from app
actions: Send GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE requests to /post
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: decision table covering all disallowed methods
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_endpoint_all_disallowed_methods_return_405():
    methods = [
        client.get,
        client.put,
        client.patch,
        client.delete,
    ]
    for method_fn in methods:
        r = method_fn('/post')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"Expected 405 but got {r.status_code}"

test_post_endpoint_all_disallowed_methods_return_405()

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_post_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Test client is created from app
actions: Send HTTP POST request to /post with JSON body {"key": "value"}
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: POST with body returns 200 and echoes JSON payload
tests.executable:
import json
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_endpoint_post_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key():
    payload = {"key": "value"}
    r = client.post(
        '/post',
        data=json.dumps(payload),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['json'] == {"key": "value"}

test_post_endpoint_post_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key()
